authoredChanges: Eight/nine slimmer connected primary arms and nested fork hierarchy replace the coarse five/six-limb crowns.
Both table assets now use connected low radial supports and dense short branch tips forming a flat-topped corymbose crown; the continuous bowl/plate surface is removed.
Massive crowns keep the original broad contact and lobed outline with bounded surface relief; open fan and rubble unchanged.
Original near triangle limit 4000, seven prototype identities and complete near/far physical fitting remain. Authored display growth forms, not named living species, measurements or scans.

limits: These are authored growth-form approximations, not living coral scans, calibrated anatomy or identified species.
Vertex colors are restrained display choices; not spectral measurements, health observations or bleaching classification.
Branch meshes intersect at connected junctions; no watertight Boolean union or pore-scale physical skeleton is claimed.
A connected radial branch and tip network approximates the table growth form; resolved corallites, fine skeletal porosity and biological branch-fusion dynamics are not modeled.
Root contact radius is measured from the normalized geometry in the lowest Y<=0.025 band; placement must still validate actual rock triangles.
Massive forms require broad near-flat support; all crown geometry remains within normalized radial XZ<=0.5 and Y0..1.
Rubble surface mottling does not resolve physical pore voids, sediment dynamics or extra ecological individuals.
USNM229 remains a separate dead skeletal specimen and is not the source of these living-display crown assets.
Offline projection shows actual triangles and vertex colors, without WebGL material, shadows, caustics or FPS verification.
previousAuthoredChanges: Batch 13 replaces both branching crowns as whole hierarchies: five or six unequal, low spreading primary limbs, three secondary forks per limb, two unequal tertiary forks per secondary, and smaller terminal side forks. Children begin on actual parent curve centrelines. Distant variants retain three/four primary limbs and fewer levels of detail.

Both table crowns replace the tall central pedestal with five low spreading support limbs and paired forks. A closed warped, scalloped fused growth surface carries short upward branch ends across its interior and edge. This is a growth-form interpretation, not a species-specific anatomical reconstruction.
Both massive crowns now have broad geometric lobes, offset shoulders and monotone meridians on a closed envelope, instead of relying on colour mottling over a regular dome.
The open reticulate fan has an uneven outline and curved shallow depth. Connected tapering branch paths remain open rather than becoming an opaque leaf sheet.

The seven shared prototype identities, existing metre-scaled scene placements, muted warm olive/brown palette and original near/distant budget remain. The five-fragment angular skeleton-rubble prototype is unchanged in this batch.
No scan, named coral species, extra biological population, scene layout change or physical growth simulation is introduced by this asset family.
